basics.name: Sarah Dury
basics.label: Plenoptic Cameras & Image-Based Rendering
basics.summary: FNRS Chargée de Recherche at LISA, Université libre de Bruxelles. Research on plenoptic camera systems, depth image-based rendering, and free-viewpoint navigation. Lead developer of the open-source Reference View Synthesis (RVS) software, adopted as the MPEG-I view synthesis reference tool; active contributor to MPEG Immersive Video standardization since 2017.

work.name: LISA, Université libre de Bruxelles
work.summary: Leading research on plenoptic 2.0 camera systems: multi-camera calibration, depth estimation, free-navigation rendering, and micro-lens design.
highlights: Supervising 3 PhD students and 2 Master thesis students on plenoptic rendering and light-field systems
Extending RVS and neural methods (NeRF, 3D Gaussian Splatting) to focused plenoptic cameras
Research stays at Nagoya University (3 months, 2024-2025) and Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (3 months, 2024)

work.name: LISA, Université libre de Bruxelles
work.summary: Developed the open-source Reference View Synthesis (RVS) software and its GPU acceleration, adopted as the official MPEG-I view synthesis tool.
highlights: Extended RVS to General Linear Camera models using Geometric Algebra
Created high-quality holographic stereograms from sparse RGBD inputs
Developed image-based rendering methods for non-Lambertian (refracting, diffracting) objects with open-source datasets
Designed a pattern-free calibration method for plenoptic 2.0 cameras
Active contributor to MPEG-I standardization (LVC, MIV, DLF subgroups), 40+ submitted documents

work.name: Iconem
work.summary: Semi-automatic registration of archive images in 3D environments for cultural heritage digitization.

work.name: French Air Force
work.summary: Software development for pilot flight preparation systems.

highlights: Supervised by Prof. Gauthier Lafruit and Prof. Mehrdad Teratani
Research on depth image-based rendering, holography, non-Lambertian rendering, and plenoptic 2.0 camera calibration
Master's thesis: 3D Reconstruction of Reflective Surfaces
